channel.title: 2026-09 on Sujith Quintelier
channel.description: Recent content in 2026-09 on Sujith Quintelier

item.title: github: Enterprise managed settings in-product validator
item.description:
GitHub Copilot now includes an in-product validator for enterprise managed settings. It checks for malformed JSON, unsupported configurations, invalid team mappings, and similar issues that could block settings from working correctly.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Usage metrics API adds pull request review stages
item.description:
GitHub’s enterprise and organization repository-level Copilot usage metrics reports now include pull request review stage timing. Each repos-1-day row gets a new pull_request_review_times array with time spent in each review stage.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Private saved views for repository issues and “Relates to” issue relationship is generally available
item.description:
GitHub repository issues now support private saved views, allowing users to save personalized issue filters and layouts. The “Relates to” issue relationship is also generally available.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Changes to query results in the GitHub Actions API and UI
item.description:
GitHub Actions workflow run queries in the API and UI now return a less precise but more accurate total count for search results across filters like workflow, event, status, and branch.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Azure HorizonDB supports PostgreSQL 18
item.description:
Azure HorizonDB is now in public preview with PostgreSQL 18 support. The service is a fully managed, PostgreSQL-compatible cloud-native database for scalable, high-performance workloads.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Agentic autofix now uses Copilot Memory
item.description:
Agentic autofix now checks Copilot Memory when that feature is enabled, using existing memories as context to help resolve security alerts.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: dotnet: AG-UI Protocol now has a first-class .NET SDK
item.description:
Microsoft released a first-class .NET SDK for the AG-UI protocol. It lets .NET services expose and consume interoperable agent endpoints through Microsoft.Extensions.AI.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot weekly releases — September 21
item.description:
GitHub Copilot’s weekly release roundup adds new models, local sandboxing in the Copilot app, and updates across Copilot integrations in Slack, Microsoft Teams, JetBrains, and VS Code.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Updates to GitHub Copilot for Slack and Microsoft Teams
item.description:
GitHub Copilot in Slack and Microsoft Teams has been updated to provide more context, more control, and a clearer path from chat conversations to GitHub work. The changelog does not include specific feature details in the provided text.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: Storm-3168: Agentic-driven cloud attacks using compromised service principals
item.description:
Microsoft describes Azure attacks linked to Storm-3168 using compromised service principals, including reconnaissance, resource deletion, and credential access. The post links the activity to JADEPUFFER and includes defender guidance.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: CodeQL 2.27.1 adds C and C++ query and Kotlin 2.4.20 support
item.description:
CodeQL 2.27.1 adds new queries for C/C++ and C#, support for Kotlin 2.4.20, and query-accuracy improvements. It is the static analysis engine used by GitHub code scanning.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Default Enablement of Copilot Features for Copilot Business and Enterprise
item.description:
GitHub is introducing a global default policy that enables generally available Copilot features and supported client capabilities in enterprise and organization Copilot settings. The change takes effect over a 28-day window.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Require proof of presence for high-impact actions
item.description:
GitHub Enterprise Cloud now supports requiring proof of presence before members perform high-impact actions. This adds an interactive re-authentication or MFA challenge on top of the existing sudo-style control.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: ai: Control where your hosted agent connects with network egress in Foundry Agent Service
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry Agent Service now supports outbound network egress controls for hosted agents. You can define and attach an outbound policy, then monitor allowed and denied calls in Audit or Enforced mode.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: azure: Retirement: Azure Communication Services (ACS) standalone services will be retired on September 30, 2028
item.description:
Microsoft will retire several standalone Azure Communication Services offerings on September 30, 2028. After that date, the affected services will no longer be available.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: commandline: Introducing run-assert-eval: Find the risk, fix it, prove it
item.description:
Microsoft introduced run-assert-eval, a skill for runtime risk discovery in agents. It identifies relevant risks, measures failure rates, generates a runtime policy from the results, and reruns evaluation to verify the fix.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Instant Access for VM restore points
item.description:
Instant Access for application-consistent restore points on Azure virtual machines is now generally available. It lets you start restoring a disk from a restore point before the underlying snapshot copy completes, for VMs using Premium SSD v2 or Ultra disks as data disks.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: security: Beyond the ransomware: Tracking Storm-2570’s consistent tradecraft across deployments
item.description:
Microsoft says Storm-2570 reuses the same post-compromise tools and techniques across multiple ransomware deployments, including Qilin, DragonForce, Anubis, and BERT. The post outlines guidance for defenders to detect and disrupt the activity before ransomware is deployed.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: ​​​​​​​​What’s new in Microsoft Security: September 2026​​
item.description:
Microsoft Security’s September 2026 update focuses on discovering and controlling local AI agents, extending Zero Trust controls to agent traffic, and improving SOC foundational capabilities.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: ai: From Chatbots to Automated Agents: Routines in Microsoft Foundry Are Now Generally Available
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry’s Routines feature is now generally available, adding event-driven and scheduled automation so agents can monitor work, react to business events, and continue tasks over time instead of only responding in chat.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: github: More ways to request and configure Copilot code reviews
item.description:
GitHub Copilot code review now supports more personal configuration options, is available to a broader set of Copilot plans, and adds an enterprise-level default setting. These changes are generally available.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Node 20 is no longer available in GitHub Actions
item.description:
GitHub Actions runners no longer include Node 20. JavaScript actions now run on Node 24, and the temporary ACTIONS_ALLOW_USE_UNSECURE_NODE_VERSION opt-out is no longer available.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: dotnet: Microsoft is updating its author-signing certificate starting September 23, 2026
item.description:
Microsoft will update the author-signing certificate used for NuGet packages on September 23, 2026. Users who rely on trusted signer policies or certificate fingerprint verification should add the new certificate before then.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: azure: Retirement: Support for PowerShell 7.4 ends on November 10, 2026
item.description:
Support for PowerShell 7.4 ends on November 10, 2026. Azure Function apps using 7.4 will keep running, but security updates and customer support stop, so users should move to PowerShell 7.6.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Retirement: Support for .NET 8 and .NET 9 ends on November 10, 2026—upgrade your apps to .NET 10
item.description:
Support for .NET 8 and .NET 9 in Azure Functions ends on November 10, 2026. Apps will keep running, but they will no longer receive security updates or support for those runtimes, so migrate to .NET 10 before the deadline.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: security: Reimagining the SOC for the agentic era in Microsoft Defender
item.description:
Microsoft announced ISOC in Microsoft Defender, a foundation for agentic security that combines SIEM and threat protection capabilities in one place. The post positions this as part of reworking the SOC for agentic-era operations.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Local sandboxing in the GitHub Copilot app
item.description:
GitHub Copilot app now supports local sandboxing to limit the impact of unintended commands by restricting access to local files, network resources, and credentials. The feature is configured in the app.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: OpenTelemetry in the GitHub Copilot app
item.description:
The GitHub Copilot app now supports OpenTelemetry configuration via enterprise-managed settings. This lets organizations observe Copilot agent performance and interactions with models and tools.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: New features and improvements in Copilot for JetBrains
item.description:
GitHub Copilot for JetBrains 1.18.0 adds AI-assisted tool approvals, more control over agent conversations, and organization-wide shared skills and instructions. It also includes plan review support with Codex.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Faster C++ code intelligence with whole codebase indexing
item.description:
GitHub Copilot CLI now supports whole-codebase indexing for C++ repositories, improving code intelligence performance. The change is aimed at large C++ codebases with many interconnected files.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: Retirement: Support for Node.js 22 ends on April 30, 2027
item.description:
Support for Node.js 22 in Azure Functions ends on April 30, 2027. Apps will keep running, but security patches, updates, and support for Node.js 22 will stop; move to Node.js 24 by then.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Flex Nodes for AKS
item.description:
Flex Nodes for AKS is now in public preview. It lets application and platform teams use hybrid and edge infrastructure as connected worker nodes to an AKS control plane in Azure, while keeping a consistent Kubernetes control plane.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: k8s: Spotlight on SIG Apps
item.description:
SIG Apps is working on workload controller reliability, node lifecycle handling, and new patterns for AI and distributed workloads while preserving backward compatibility. The article highlights current focus areas, the trade-offs in changing core APIs, and a proposed Job API update for Kubernetes 1.38.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: github: Claude Opus 5.5 is now available in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
Claude Opus 5.5 is now available in GitHub Copilot. GitHub says it can be used for agentic coding, long-running agentic tasks, and knowledge work.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: dotnet: Creating a memory dump in C#
item.description:
The post describes how to create a memory dump from a C# application for debugging. It focuses on capturing the app’s state so it can be analyzed later.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: github: OpenAI’s GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna now available
item.description:
GitHub Copilot now includes two additional OpenAI GPT-6 models: GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna. They join the previously available GPT-6 Astra as selectable model options.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: Unmasking EvilTokens: Getting to the root of device code phishing
item.description:
Microsoft says it helped disrupt EvilTokens, a phishing-as-a-service platform used for device code phishing and token theft. The post describes AI-assisted lures, automated infrastructure, and Microsoft DCU’s role in the disruption.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: devops+ai: Full SDLC in a Single Skill Command
item.description:
The article title and subtitle suggest a workflow for managing the full software development lifecycle from Jira to production using a single command and a team of automated agents. No technical implementation details are provided in the excerpt.

  • Source: Let’s do DevOps

item.title: github: Security improvements for SSH
item.description:
GitHub is updating SSH security by removing several older algorithms, adding a new one, and requiring larger RSA SSH keys. The change tightens supported SSH configurations to improve security.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Deprecation notice: All-platform CodeQL bundle
item.description:
GitHub has deprecated the all-platform CodeQL bundle starting with CodeQL CLI 2.27.0. The deprecated artifacts are codeql-bundle.tar.gz and codeql-bundle.tar.zst, which previously included binaries for all supported platforms.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Refreshed repository pull requests page generally available
item.description:
GitHub has generally available a refreshed repository pull requests page for all users. The update is intended to make pull requests easier to find and act on from one place.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Enterprise adds credential inventory exports
item.description:
GitHub Enterprise now lets enterprise owners export a complete inventory of credentials that can access the enterprise. The export includes SSH keys, classic and fine-grained personal access tokens, OAuth App access tokens, and other credential types.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Sphere OS version 26.09 is now available
item.description:
Azure Sphere OS version 26.09 is now available in the Retail feed. This release updates only the OS; there is no SDK update, and internet-connected devices will receive it from the cloud.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: k8s: Kubernetes v1.37: Tracking When a PersistentVolumeClaim Was Last Used (Beta)
item.description:
Kubernetes v1.37 promotes PersistentVolumeClaimUnusedSinceTime to Beta and enables it by default. PVCs now get an Unused condition in status so you can tell whether any running or pending pod references the claim, and use lastTransitionTime to see when it last became idle.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Introducing a Guided Copilot Experience for Building Azure Apps in VS Code
item.description:
Microsoft is previewing a guided Copilot experience in VS Code for building Azure apps. It provides a structured workflow that helps move from idea to deployed app instead of relying on a free-form chat session.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Functions support for PowerShell 7.6
item.description:
Azure Functions now generally supports PowerShell 7.6. Apps can be developed locally with PowerShell 7.6 and deployed to Azure Functions plans.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Grok 4.7 is now available in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
Grok 4.7 is rolling out in GitHub Copilot. GitHub describes it as xAI’s latest reasoning model, intended for agentic coding and complex multistep workflows.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot code review: An improved review experience
item.description:
GitHub updated Copilot code review to make review changes easier to track over time, auto-resolve more of its own suggestions, and generate commit messages when suggestions are accepted.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Manage the code coverage ruleset condition with the REST API
item.description:
GitHub now supports managing the “Restrict code coverage” repository ruleset option through the generally available REST API, in addition to the existing UI. This lets admins enforce code coverage requirements programmatically.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot weekly releases — September 14
item.description:
GitHub Copilot’s weekly release adds new model selection options, updates to code review, and Sentry integration in the Copilot app. The post also mentions additional admin updates and new agent features.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Foundry Routines in Foundry Agent Service
item.description:
Foundry Agent Service now includes Foundry Routines in public preview. This adds a native trigger primitive so published agents can run automatically on schedules or in response to business events.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Upcoming deprecation of selected GitHub Copilot models in mid-October
item.description:
GitHub will deprecate selected Copilot models across all Copilot experiences on October 19, 2026. The affected models include those used in Copilot Chat, inline edits, ask and agent modes, and code completions.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Mdsv4 and Msv4 Series Virtual Machines for SAP
item.description:
Azure announced public preview availability of the Mdsv4 and Msv4 memory-optimized virtual machine series for SAP. The series uses 6th Generation Intel Xeon Scalable processors and includes advanced security features plus Azure Boost technologies.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Enable and disable controls for Microsoft Foundry agents in Agent 365
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry agents can now be enabled or disabled from the Agent 365 governance surface in Microsoft Admin Center, and the feature is generally available. Administrators can control whether a Foundry agent is available for use across the tenant.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Network egress controls for hosted agents in Microsoft Foundry
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry public preview now supports network egress controls for hosted agents. Customers can define ordered outbound rules by destination host, including wildcard FQDNs like *.contoso.com, with allow or deny actions.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Publishing Microsoft Foundry agents to Microsoft 365 Copilot and Teams
item.description:
Publishing Microsoft Foundry agents to Microsoft 365 Copilot and Teams is now generally available. This gives Foundry developers a native path to make agents operational in the Microsoft 365 surfaces where users work.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Logical replication slot sync status metric for Azure PostgreSQL Flexible Server
item.description:
Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server now includes a new Azure Monitor metric, logical_replication_slot_sync_status, to track the synchronization status of logical replication slots. It is generally available and lets you monitor whether each logical replication slot is in sync.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Stage-only npm tokens for safer automation
item.description:
GitHub added a new npm granular access token permission option, Read and write (stage only). It allows automated workflows to stage package versions for review without granting the token full publish access.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: New and improved troubleshooting guides for Azure Database for PostgreSQL
item.description:
Updated troubleshooting guidance is now available for Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server. The documentation adds expanded diagnostics for high CPU, memory, IOPS, temporary file usage, and autovacuum issues to help identify root causes.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: PG18 support for Azure Database for PostgreSQL elastic clusters
item.description:
Azure Database for PostgreSQL elastic clusters now support PostgreSQL 18. The update is available generally and is intended for new or existing distributed, cloud-scale workloads.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Copilot impact dashboard now shows feature engagement
item.description:
The Copilot impact dashboard now includes feature engagement data, showing how many active users regularly use key Copilot features. Enterprise administrators can use it to identify widely adopted experiences and those that may need more attention.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Agentic CLI customizations now in the usage metrics API
item.description:
GitHub Copilot’s usage metrics API now includes agentic CLI activity for skills, custom agents, MCP servers, slash commands, and plugins. This extends existing CLI report coverage with additional customization metrics.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Azure Payments HSM v2
item.description:
Azure Payments HSM v2 is in public preview. It is a highly available, single-tenant payment HSM service for payment processing, credential issuance, PIN processing, key management, and authentication data protection, with exclusive administrative control retained by the customer.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: High-scale mesh in Azure Virtual Network Manager
item.description:
High-scale mesh connectivity with connected groups in Azure Virtual Network Manager is now generally available. In supported regions, a single mesh connectivity configuration can connect up to 3,000 virtual networks by default, with higher scale IP connectivity available.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: security: From guidance to action: Security fundamentals that materially reduce risk
item.description:
Microsoft says AI has changed the cybersecurity operating environment and points readers to exposure management guidance with recommended controls. The post emphasizes taking action on security fundamentals to reduce risk.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Ubuntu 26 generally available and latest migration
item.description:
Ubuntu 26.04 runner images for GitHub Actions are now generally available and fully supported for production workflows on x64 and arm64. The release notes also mention a migration update.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: Improving email security outcomes with real-world Microsoft Defender insights
item.description:
Microsoft says its latest email security benchmarking reports show strong Defender performance in both pre-delivery and post-delivery scenarios. The post also notes ongoing changes in how threats and defenses are evolving.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Workflow execution protections in GitHub Actions generally available
item.description:
Workflow execution protections in GitHub Actions are now generally available for GitHub Enterprise, organizations, and repositories. The feature lets you define an allowlist to control who can execute workflows.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: dotnet: Build Your Own AI Agent Harness in C#, the MafClaw Live Series
item.description:
Microsoft is running a 4-part live series showing how to build a C# AI agent harness with Microsoft Agent Framework, starting from a single IChatClient call and evolving it into a production-ready agent with observability and governance. The post is an announcement for the series and does not include technical implementation details.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: github: Automate SSO authorization for classic PATs and SSH keys
item.description:
GitHub Enterprise Cloud now lets enterprise admins automate SSO authorization for existing classic PATs and SSH keys across organizations, removing the need for developers to authorize each org manually.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: SCIM user responses now include a profileUrl attribute
item.description:
GitHub SCIM user responses now include the RFC 7643 standard profileUrl attribute. It returns the absolute URL of the GitHub account linked to the external identity.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot budget increase requests are generally available
item.description:
GitHub Copilot now supports a request flow for users who have exhausted their AI credits, allowing them to ask for a budget increase instead of being fully blocked from credit-consuming features. The feature is now generally available.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: k8s: Kubernetes v1.37: Hardening Container Storage with Bind Mount Options and EmptyDir Permissions
item.description:
Kubernetes v1.37 adds alpha support for bind mount options on volume mounts and configurable permission modes for emptyDir volumes. These features let users apply Linux mount flags like noexec, nosuid, and nodev, and set emptyDir modes such as 01777 or 0750 without init-container workarounds.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: azure: Retirement Update: SAP container images removed October 14, 2026
item.description:
SAP container images are scheduled for removal on October 14, 2026. The containerized SAP data connector retired on September 14, 2026 and is now unsupported and unmaintained, though existing TLS-compliant agents can still send logs through the retired HTTP Data Collector API.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Azure SQL updates for mid-September 2026
item.description:
Azure SQL added a public preview for soft delete on logical servers. When a logical server is deleted, it enters a soft-deleted state and can be restored within the configured window.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Azure Red Hat OpenShift with hosted control planes
item.description:
Azure Red Hat OpenShift with hosted control planes is now in public preview. This deployment option separates the OpenShift control plane into a fully managed service from the worker nodes that run customer workloads.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: PostgreSQL skills and MCP plugin for Azure Database for PostgreSQL
item.description:
Microsoft previewed PostgreSQL skills and an MCP plugin for Azure Database for PostgreSQL. The plugin is intended to make supported AI coding assistants context-aware for PostgreSQL and able to provide guidance and perform actions on a connected database.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Code scanning AI Scan no longer requires CodeQL default setup
item.description:
AI Scan for pull requests can now find security vulnerabilities even when CodeQL default setup is not enabled on a repository. Previously, AI Scan for pull requests required CodeQL default setup.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Enforce GitHub Advanced Security configurations
item.description:
Enterprise administrators can now enforce GitHub Advanced Security configurations at the enterprise level. This blocks organization and repository administrators from changing those settings.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot suggests custom properties definitions
item.description:
GitHub Copilot can now suggest allowed values when creating custom properties for repositories in an organization. The feature is in public preview for GitHub Copilot Business and Copilot users.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: ai: Introducing Foundry Dev Pack: One Command to Start Building
item.description:
Microsoft announced Foundry Dev Pack, an all-in-one installer that prepares a machine for Microsoft Foundry development. It installs the tools needed for use in the terminal, VS Code, and coding agents.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: k8s: Kubernetes v1.37: Pod-Level Resource Managers graduated to Beta
item.description:
Kubernetes v1.37 graduates Pod-Level Resource Managers to Beta, disabled by default behind the PodLevelResourceManagers feature gate. Kubelet’s Topology Manager, CPU Manager, and Memory Manager can now use pod-level resource declarations for NUMA-aware placement, and the PodResources API reports top-level CPU and memory assignments.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: github: SHA-1 in HTTPS on GitHub sunset
item.description:
GitHub has completed the scheduled sunset of SHA-1 for HTTPS on github.com and partner services. SHA-1 is now disabled for HTTPS connections.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: devops+ai: 🔥AI makes works for itself
item.description:
The note says AI should be used to update tools, and nothing more. It frames the idea as “AI to update tools only.”

  • Source: Let’s do DevOps

item.title: dotnet: Performance Improvements in .NET 11
item.description:
The post says .NET 11 includes hundreds of performance improvements and invites readers to review them in detail. No specific runtime, libraries, or API changes are listed in the provided text.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: k8s: Kubernetes Changed Block Tracking API - Beta Differences
item.description:
Kubernetes changed block tracking for CSI drivers is now Beta with external-snapshot-metadata v1.0.0. The main Beta change is promotion of SnapshotMetadataService from cbt.storage.k8s.io/v1alpha1 to v1beta1, with no schema change but no served v1alpha1 version.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: k8s: Kubernetes v1.37: Memory QoS Graduates to Beta
item.description:
Kubernetes v1.37 makes Memory QoS Beta and turns it on by default, but it does not change runtime behavior unless you explicitly set throttling or reservation fields. The main config change is that memoryThrottlingFactor now defaults to null, so existing clusters will not start writing memory.high unless they already set it.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: azure: Announcing: New Windows App client-side endpoints for Azure Virtual Desktop
item.description:
Windows App will start using three new wildcard FQDNs for client-side service traffic to Azure Virtual Desktop beginning in early October 2026. The domains are already part of the cloud-side connectivity requirements.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: HTTP/3 over QUIC support in Azure Application Gateway
item.description:
Azure Application Gateway now has public preview support for HTTP/3 over QUIC. The update is intended to improve connection setup time, reduce latency, and increase resiliency for web applications and APIs.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: dotnet: Share your .NET story with the community
item.description:
Microsoft is asking the community to share real-world .NET usage stories from teams and projects. The goal is to collect examples for .NET Conf 2026 and other .NET channels.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: github: Configure cost and quality in Copilot auto model selection
item.description:
GitHub Copilot auto model selection now has three tiers: efficiency, balance, and intelligence. These let you choose how auto weighs cost, quality, and response time.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Profiles now show your highest achievement badge tier
item.description:
GitHub profiles now display the highest tier earned for achievements that have multiple levels. Before this change, profiles could show the first tier earned even after a user progressed further.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Add VS Code Agents to Copilot usage metrics
item.description:
GitHub Copilot usage metrics now include generally available activity metrics for the dedicated VS Code Agents window. This lets enterprises and organizations track adoption and engagement for VS Code Agents alongside other Copilot usage.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Auto-resolution and analysis updates in Copilot code review
item.description:
Copilot code review now auto-resolves its own comments after you address them, and it can generate commit messages when you apply its code suggestions. The update also includes behind-the-scenes analysis changes.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: k8s: Kubernetes v1.37: Native Histograms Graduates to Beta
item.description:
Kubernetes v1.37 enables native histogram support for metrics by default and moves the feature to Beta. Components now dual-expose classic buckets and native spans, and users must adjust Prometheus scraping and queries depending on Prometheus version.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: azure: Retirement: Azure Linux with OS Guard in Azure Kubernetes Service
item.description:
Support for Azure Linux with OS Guard in Azure Kubernetes Service ends on December 10, 2026. After that date, new Azure Linux with OS Guard clusters cannot be created, and Azure Container Linux is the replacement.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Agentless migration of on-premises SMB file shares to Azure Files (SMB)
item.description:
Azure Storage Mover now supports agentless migration of on-premises SMB file shares to Azure Files (SMB) in public preview. The migration can move data from Windows Server or NAS shares without deploying, registering, or maintaining a migration agent.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot weekly releases — September 7
item.description:
GitHub Copilot’s Sept. 7 weekly release adds Jira integration in Copilot app and adaptive model orchestration via Project HydraFusion in Copilot CLI. It also introduces new agent automation in Visual Studio Code.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Refreshed repository pull requests page in public preview
item.description:
GitHub is previewing a refreshed repository-level pull request listing page for all users. The update adds stronger filtering and a compact presentation mode.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: AI Scan for pull request APIs in public preview
item.description:
GitHub code scanning’s AI Scan for pull request feature can now be enabled and managed via REST API at both the organization and repository levels. The APIs are in public preview.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: k8s: Kubernetes v1.37: Scheduler Preemption for In-Place Pod Resize (Alpha)
item.description:
Kubernetes v1.37 adds alpha support for scheduler preemption during in-place Pod resize, gated by InPlacePodVerticalScalingSchedulerPreemption. If a running Pod’s resize is Deferred due to lack of node capacity, the scheduler can now preempt lower-priority Pods on the same node so the resize can complete without restarting the Pod.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: ai: Announcing Azure AI Speech LLM 2607: Better Multilingual Accuracy, Easier Customization
item.description:
Azure AI Speech LLM 2607 adds improved multilingual and mixed-language recognition, lower latency, and simpler domain-specific customization through enhanced phrase lists. The release focuses on accuracy and customization for speech recognition workloads.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: github: Control GitHub Actions cache access with cache-mode
item.description:
GitHub Actions now supports cache-mode to control cache access at the workflow or job level. This lets you grant least-privilege cache access instead of broad cache permissions.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: Protecting organizations from AI-assisted executive impersonation and invoice fraud
item.description:
Microsoft describes an AI-assisted business email compromise campaign that impersonated executives and used fake invoices to target finance teams for ACH payment fraud. The post focuses on the attack pattern and how organizations can protect against it.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: dotnet: Use C# unions and closed hierarchies in ASP.NET Core
item.description:
The post explains how C# unions and closed hierarchies integrate with System.Text.Json in ASP.NET Core. It covers use across Minimal APIs, MVC, SignalR, Blazor, and OpenAPI.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: github: MAI-Code-1-Flash deprecated
item.description:
GitHub deprecated MAI-Code-1-Flash across all Copilot experiences on September 10, 2026. The suggested alternative is referenced in the deprecation notice.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: TLS/SSL certificate and end-to-end TLS encryption support for Azure Functions Flex Consumption
item.description:
Azure Functions Flex Consumption now generally supports TLS/SSL certificates using a new site-scoped certificate model. It also adds end-to-end TLS encryption support for function apps in this plan.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: security: Detect and disrupt AI-themed attacks with Microsoft Defender
item.description:
Microsoft Defender is described as detecting and disrupting AI-themed phishing, malware, and multi-stage attacks across the attack chain. The post is a Microsoft Security Blog entry dated 2026-09-10.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Copilot Troubleshooting Agent
item.description:
Azure Copilot Troubleshooting Agent is now generally available. It provides a built-in Azure Copilot capability for investigating and resolving operational issues, and is available through Azure Copilot and Support.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Xcode 27 runner image now runs on macOS 27
item.description:
GitHub’s Xcode 27 runner image for GitHub-hosted macOS runners now runs on macOS 27 and is available in public preview. This lets you validate Apple apps against macOS 27 using that runner image.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: commandline: PyRIT: Democratizing AI red teaming through open-source tooling
item.description:
PyRIT is presented as an open-source Python tool for AI red teaming that lowers the barrier for subject matter experts to test generative AI systems. The article describes its evolution toward making red teaming more accessible across many domains.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: ai: What’s new in Microsoft Foundry: July and August 2026
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry’s July and August 2026 update adds stable Hosted Agent and Toolbox SDK paths, Claude tools support on Azure-hosted deployments, and Model Router updates. It also notes local inference improvements and SDK migration items to review before upgrading.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: User-bound user delegation SAS for Azure Storage
item.description:
Azure Storage now generally available with user-bound user delegation SAS, combining user delegation SAS flexibility with Entra ID user-bound access for stronger authentication. The update adds enhanced secure authentication for Azure Storage.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: npm extends recovery-code security holds to all accounts
item.description:
npm now applies a 72-hour security hold to any account after a successful recovery-code sign-in. The hold was previously limited to high-impact accounts.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: CodeQL 2.27.0 adds support for Linux ARM64
item.description:
CodeQL 2.27.0 is available on Linux ARM64. The release also adds a new Rust security query, expands framework coverage for Java/Kotlin and C#, and includes analysis accuracy improvements across multiple languages.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: Threat matrix: Mapping threats across cloud web applications
item.description:
Microsoft introduced the Cloud Web Applications Threat Matrix, a MITRE ATT&CK-aligned framework for understanding and prioritizing threats against cloud-hosted web applications and serverless platforms. It is intended to help defenders map attacks and identify mitigations.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Ephemeral OS Disk with full caching for VM/VMSS
item.description:
Azure Ephemeral OS Disk with full caching is now generally available for new virtual machines and Virtual Machine Scale Sets. It caches the full OS image on local VM storage so reads no longer go to remote storage after caching completes.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Enterprise managed permissions for GitHub Copilot agent operations
item.description:
GitHub Copilot Business and Enterprise admins can now centrally manage agent operation permissions. Admins can set operations to be blocked, require human approval, or run without prompting.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: k8s: Kubernetes v1.37: Introducing Node Lifecycle Conditions
item.description:
Kubernetes v1.37 reserves five well-known Node lifecycle condition types and adds an alpha feature gate for future built-in behavior, but the gate is disabled by default and no core components act on the conditions yet. The release is meant to provide a shared, Kubernetes-owned signal for drains, maintenance, and graceful shutdown so operators and external controllers can report Node lifecycle state consistently.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: security: Passkey-themed social engineering leads to identity and cloud compromise
item.description:
Microsoft describes a threat campaign using passkey-themed social engineering to compromise identities and extend access into cloud services. The activity includes MFA persistence, Microsoft Graph reconnaissance, and access to SharePoint, OneDrive, and email data, with guidance on detection and mitigation.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: GitHub Advanced Security expands trial availability
item.description:
GitHub Advanced Security self-serve trials are now available to more GitHub Enterprise Cloud customers. The trial can be used to evaluate GitHub Code Security and GitHub Secret Protection.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Block pull requests with exposed secrets from merging
item.description:
GitHub added a repository ruleset capability to prevent pull requests from merging when they introduce exposed secrets. This extends rulesets as a repository-wide protection mechanism.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Remediate Code Quality findings with agentic autofix
item.description:
GitHub added agentic autofix for Code Quality findings, allowing users to select and assign up to 25 standard findings at once for automated remediation. The feature is aimed at reducing backlog items in code quality reports.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: aks: Release 2026-09-04
item.description:
AKS release v20260904 rolls out Kubernetes 1.37 preview, adds GA autoscaling for VM node pools, and includes updates across gateway, service mesh, CSI, and cloud-provider components. It also introduces several behavioral changes, bug fixes, and retirement notices for VMAS clusters and Azure Linux with OS Guard.

  • Source: Release notes from AKS

item.title: github: Enterprise-managed sandbox in Copilot for JetBrains
item.description:
Copilot for JetBrains now supports enterprise-managed sandbox policies, along with cross-file cursor jumps for next edit suggestions, global project context in chat, and enterprise policy diagnostics. The update also adds a new terminal Copilot connection.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Enterprise Server 3.22 is now generally available
item.description:
GitHub Enterprise Server 3.22 is generally available. The release adds new platform capabilities, including administrator configuration for Copilot CLI.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: dotnet: Announcing .NET 11 Release Candidate 1
item.description:
The .NET 11 Release Candidate 1 is now available. The release includes updates across libraries, runtime, SDK, MSBuild, NuGet, C#, F#, ASP.NET Core, .NET MAUI, and Windows Forms.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: dotnet: .NET Conf 2026 Community Days Call for Presenters Is Open
item.description:
The call for presenters is open for .NET Conf 2026 Community Days. Session proposals are due by October 6, 2026.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: dotnet: .NET and .NET Framework September 2026 servicing releases updates
item.description:
The post announces the September 2026 servicing updates for .NET and .NET Framework. It is a recap of the latest servicing releases, but the provided text does not include version numbers or fixes.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: k8s: Kubernetes v1.37: Advancing Workload-Aware Scheduling
item.description:
Kubernetes v1.37 advances Workload-Aware Scheduling: Workload and PodGroup APIs, gang scheduling, workload-aware preemption, and shared DRA ResourceClaims graduate to Beta. It also introduces Alpha support for CompositePodGroup and multi-level topology-aware scheduling, plus new controller integration APIs and Job controller integration for explicit WAS configuration.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: github: New customer portal help.github.com
item.description:
GitHub moved and redesigned its support portal to help.github.com. The new portal combines support, documentation, learning, community, account resources, and Copilot-powered search in one place.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Playwright Workspaces in Australia East, Japan East, and Switzerland North
item.description:
Playwright Workspaces in Azure App Testing is now generally available in Switzerland North, Japan East, and Australia East. It provides managed cloud-hosted browsers for running Playwright end-to-end tests at scale with parallel execution.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Developer CLI (azd) Extension Framework
item.description:
The Azure Developer CLI (azd) Extension Framework is now generally available. It lets developers, teams, and partners extend azd with custom capabilities for their application development workflows.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot weekly releases — August 31
item.description:
GitHub Copilot’s latest weekly release adds more model choice and content protection controls. VS Code also gets new options for managing agent sessions and preparing pull requests for merge.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: How to secure edge AI in customer-owned environments
item.description:
Microsoft says edge AI deployments in customer-owned environments require stronger verification of systems, software, and AI assets before sharing sensitive data, credentials, or models. The post frames secure edge AI as a trust and validation problem for third-party environments.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: GPT-6 Astra is generally available in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
GPT-6 Astra from OpenAI is now generally available in GitHub Copilot. GitHub says the model is intended for long-horizon, autonomous coding and agentic tasks.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: k8s: Kubernetes v1.37: KubeletInUserNamespace (aka Rootless mode) Graduates to Beta
item.description:
Kubernetes v1.37 moves KubeletInUserNamespace to beta and enables the feature gate by default. It allows node components to run as a non-root user in a Linux user namespace, reducing host impact from node-component exploits, while leaving existing rootful clusters unchanged unless explicitly configured.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: github: New API endpoint provides privacy-safe star history data
item.description:
GitHub added a new REST API endpoint for repository star history that lets users track star growth over time without exposing individual stargazer identities. This follows earlier restrictions on stargazer listing endpoints to admins and collaborators.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Multiple trusted publishing configurations for npm
item.description:
GitHub says three npm publishing updates are now generally available, including support for multiple trusted publishing configurations per package. The post also mentions staged publishing and another publishing-related change, but the provided excerpt does not include the full details.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Actions: Early September 2026 updates
item.description:
GitHub Actions added three updates focused on workflow visibility and control. The post highlights a new REST API for runner version deprecations, but the provided excerpt does not include the full details of the other changes.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Upcoming deprecation of selected GitHub Copilot models
item.description:
GitHub will deprecate selected Copilot models across all Copilot experiences on October 2, 2026. The affected models include Copilot Chat, inline edits, ask and agent modes, and code completions.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub CLI Linux package signing key expires September 5
item.description:
The GitHub CLI Linux package repository signing key expires on September 5, 2026. After that date, repository metadata in APT and RPM workflows will be affected starting with the first release published after expiration.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Gemini 3.8 Flash is now available in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
GitHub Copilot now supports Gemini 3.8 Flash, Google’s latest Flash model. GitHub says early testing showed strong performance on complex terminal-based coding tasks.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: k8s: Kubernetes v1.37: DRA Updates
item.description:
Kubernetes 1.37 adds several DRA updates, including GA support for extended resources, stable device taints/tolerations, and stable standardized NUMA node attributes. It also promotes multiple DRA features to Beta or Alpha, with focus areas including workload-level ResourceClaims, device metadata/status, scheduling performance, and fractional consumable capacity.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: dotnet: Test what you ship: MSTest and Native AOT
item.description:
MSTest source generation now lets test projects run with the same Native AOT and trimming deployment model as the apps they validate. It also reduces reflection on the test execution path.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Virtual Network Manager IPAM in additional Azure regions
item.description:
Azure Virtual Network Manager IP address management is now generally available in additional regions: US Gov Virginia, US Gov Texas, US Gov Arizona, China North 3, and China East 3.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: security: ASCII smuggling crosses over from AI prompt injection to phishing evasion
item.description:
Microsoft reports that invisible Unicode characters, previously used in AI prompt injection, are now being used to hide words from email filters as part of phishing evasion. The technique relies on obfuscating text before parsers process it.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Reopening Copilot Business and Enterprise signups
item.description:
GitHub is gradually reopening sign-ups for Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise for customers paying by credit card or PayPal over the next few weeks. Availability is rolling out gradually to people who have been waiting to start.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: CodeQL 2.26.4 improves GitHub actions security detections
item.description:
CodeQL 2.26.4 is a new release that adds support for Go 1.27 and improves GitHub Actions security detections. It is part of the static analysis engine used by GitHub code scanning.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: Impersonating IT support: how threat actors turn a remote session into enterprise-wide access
item.description:
Microsoft Threat Intelligence reported a human-operated intrusion campaign that abuses Microsoft Teams external collaboration to impersonate IT support, gain remote access, and deploy a Node.js-based implant. The campaign uses social engineering and legitimate tools to move from initial access to lateral movement, with Microsoft Defender used for detection and disruption.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Enterprise-managed settings support any default model
item.description:
Enterprise-managed settings can now set any supported GitHub Copilot model as the default for new conversations. This lets enterprises choose the default model that best matches their workflow.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: k8s: Kubernetes v1.37: Scale Workloads to Zero with HorizontalPodAutoscaler
item.description:
Kubernetes v1.37 makes HorizontalPodAutoscaler scale workloads down to zero replicas by default when using object or external metrics. The feature is Beta; it requires a metric source that remains available at zero replicas, and the controller marks zero-state ownership with a ScaledToZero condition.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: github: Content exclusions generally available in Copilot app and CLI
item.description:
GitHub Copilot app and CLI now honor content exclusion policies set at the enterprise, organization, and repository levels. Excluded files will not be used as context by Copilot.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Azure Front Door profile and route level WAF policies
item.description:
Azure Front Door Web Application Firewall (WAF) now supports associating WAF policies at the profile and route levels in public preview. This lets you apply baseline protection across a profile and more targeted policies on specific routes.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Reader Endpoint for Azure Database for MySQL
item.description:
Azure Database for MySQL - Flexible Server now has a public preview of a reader endpoint to simplify connection management when using multiple replicas. The endpoint provides automatic load balancing for read-only connections.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: security: Counterfeit installers to system compromise: Tracking a deceptive software download campaign
item.description:
Microsoft describes an active malware campaign that uses fake software download pages and repackaged installer archives to impersonate legitimate vendors. The post includes observed tactics, Defender XDR detections, indicators of compromise, and mitigation guidance.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Microsoft Defender for Cloud support for Azure Container Apps (Serverless Containers Posture)
item.description:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud now supports Azure Container Apps environments in its Serverless Containers Posture experience. This lets security teams manage posture for more of their container estate from one workflow.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Windows Server 2025 on AKS
item.description:
AKS now supports Windows Server 2025 in general availability, giving customers a newer Windows node option for Windows-based Kubernetes workloads on Azure. This is intended to help with modernization as older Windows Server versions near retirement.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Artifact Streaming on AKS
item.description:
Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) now supports Artifact streaming with Azure Container Registry (ACR) in generally available form. It is intended to reduce wait time when starting containerized workloads by allowing images to be used before they are fully pulled.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Confidential VMs for Azure Linux
item.description:
Confidential Virtual Machines for Azure Linux in AKS are now generally available. This adds CVM node pool support for migrating highly sensitive container workloads to AKS.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Enterprise Live Migrations from GHES to ghe.com generally available
item.description:
Enterprise Live Migrations is now generally available for near-zero-downtime repository migrations from GitHub Enterprise Server (GHES) to GitHub Enterprise Cloud with Data Residency (GHEC DR).

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Set an expiration date for individual user budgets
item.description:
GitHub now lets you set an optional expiration date on an individual user budget. When the date is reached, GitHub automatically removes the budget; the feature is generally available.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot code review can now approve pull requests
item.description:
Copilot code review can now indicate when a pull request is ready for approval, and repository admins can authorize it to approve the PR. The approval capability is disabled by default.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: Cybersecurity IR Workshop: The workshop you shouldn’t miss
item.description:
Microsoft Security blog post promoting a cybersecurity incident response workshop focused on preparedness and response. It says the workshop shares practical insights from DART to improve cyber resilience before a crisis.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Purchase order mapping available in Microsoft Marketplace
item.description:
Microsoft Marketplace purchase order mapping is now generally available. It lets organizations allocate Microsoft invoices, including Marketplace purchases, to support accounting and reconciliation of cloud and AI spend.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: k8s: Kubernetes v1.37: etcd RangeStream Cuts Memory Use on Large List Reads
item.description:
Kubernetes v1.37 graduates the EtcdRangeStream feature to beta and enables it by default. With etcd v3.7+, the API server can stream large collection reads instead of assembling whole pages in memory, reducing peak memory use and making it more predictable.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Firewall auto-learn SNAT routes
item.description:
Azure Firewall auto-learn SNAT routes is now generally available. It periodically learns registered and private destination prefixes and applies them as No-SNAT ranges to preserve original source IPs and reduce manual SNAT management.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Copilot Observability Agent supports Basic and Auxiliary table plans
item.description:
Azure Copilot Observability Agent now supports Log Analytics data stored in Basic and Auxiliary table plans for interactive analysis and deep investigations. This extends coverage to high-volume telemetry in Azure Monitor.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Block users from discussion comments in personal repositories
item.description:
GitHub added in-context blocking controls for discussion comments in repositories owned by personal accounts. Users can now block or unblock other users directly from discussion comments, matching the existing issue and pull request comment behavior.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Monitor Auxiliary Logs Plan in Azure Government and China regions
item.description:
Azure Monitor Auxiliary Logs Plan is now generally available in Azure Government (Fairfax) and China regions. The plan is intended for cost-effective ingestion and retention of high-volume, verbose logs for compliance and auditing.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Monitor Auxiliary Logs Plan support for Azure tables and plan switching
item.description:
Azure Monitor Logs Auxiliary table plan now supports Azure tables and switching plans, and both capabilities are generally available. The plan is intended for high-volume, low-query logs used for compliance and auditing.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Claude Fable 5.1 is generally available in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
Claude Fable 5.1 from Anthropic is now generally available in GitHub Copilot. GitHub says it is intended for long-horizon, autonomous coding and knowledge-work tasks.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub CLI: Media in issues, pull requests, and comments
item.description:
GitHub CLI now supports a repeatable --attach flag to upload local images or videos and insert them inline in issue, pull request, or comment bodies. This adds media attachment support to GitHub CLI posts and comments.

  • Source: GitHub
